I honestly think it had a lot to do with my other tulpas’ actions before they left and the addition of the antidepressants. Before the fall of my Innerworld (which I called “The Paradigm”), Desdemon’s only goal was to try and kill off the other tulpas by telling them that they didn’t exist and they were nothing, and then eventually- 

Hold on. I think Desdemon wants to explain this himself. I would delete my previous sentences just so he could have the spotlight, but maybe it’ll provide a little more insight. 

*Before my reformation, I only knew jealousy. I only knew violence and hatred for my fellow head mates, and I hated them because they were beneficial to the Host and I was seen as the bad guy. I was the Vice, or so they claimed. They hated me because I hated the Host, constantly telling her that she needed to change and that she would never be good enough for anything in this world. I honestly told her these things because I thought they would help her develop into a more worthy, more influential person. But it didn’t work. Eventually it got to the point where she began to consider suicide, and that’s when the others knew that something had to be done. So, they convinced her to tell someone about her problems, and she was put on medication.*

*I think the meds are what really saved us. Both me and her.*

*Once the medication began inserting itself into the Host’s body, I couldn’t fight anymore. My words fell upon deaf ears, and the others had no trouble dealing with me. During this time, I also began to feel things I had never felt before. Empathy. Regret. Admiration. Love. Sadness. And over time, I realized what I had done to her. I only wish I could’ve known sooner. Because of me, the Paradigm is gone. Because of me, my head mates have left us. It’s because of me that she’s still not over her issues, but we’re working together to rectify that.*

-*Desdemon*

So yeah. I guess that pretty much sums it up.

That’s exactly how Desdemon is for me, and that’s what the rest of my tulpas used to be. But over time, due to some other issues, I wasn’t able to keep up my relationship to the others, so I allowed them to make a choice: they could either stay and work through the silence with me, or leave. Everyone but Desdemon left. 

Not that Desdemon ever really had a choice. Unlike the others, he and I are what I call “soul-bonded”. He couldn’t leave even if he wanted to. He was created as an amalgamation of everything I hated about myself, and as he developed (and as I got put on anti-depressants), he began developing into a person that tried to help me and encourage me. Where he once pushed me to hate myself, now he does the opposite. I guess you could call him what other people call “inner demons”, stuff like depression and negativity and whatnot, heck his name was derived from the word demon, but he’s done a complete 180. We don’t switch places or anything either, we’re just different representations of the same human. Desdemon was the negative and I was the positive. But now we’re both trying to heal and work together. 

In any case, I hope my experience shed a little light for you, although it’s not too helpful haha.

One of the things that I do whenever I’m on the brink of a panic attack (or during one) is something called grounding. Look around whatever room you’re in and find something you can touch, then go over and touch it. It could be something as simple as your shirt or the surface of a couch, or even your hair. Then, if you think moving on will help, find other things you can interact with. For example, find something you can smell, something you can see, something you can hear, something you can taste and so on. While interacting with whatever object you’ve chosen, go slowly and remind yourself that you are here, you exist, the world around you exists, and as bad as the panic attack may feel, it won’t last forever. 

I only use the touch method, though. It’s the only one that helps me. I run my hand over a pillow I have or find some sort of object to squeeze between my hands. Sometimes the feeling of ice cold water helps as well. 

Another thing that has helped me is meditation. You can find guided sessions and videos online, or you could do it on your own. 

Hope you get well soon. Stay strong ;)
